sources.title: Benchmark Contamination in LLMs - Complete Guide | AI Wiki
sources.snippet: Benchmark contamination occurs when test data from evaluation benchmarks appears in a language model's training set, artificially inflating performance metrics and undermining the validity of model comparisons. This issue has become increasingly prevalent as models are trained on larger web-scraped datasets that may inadvertently include publicly available benchmark questions.

sources.title: Benchmark Contamination in AI: When Tests Leak Into Training
sources.snippet: Benchmark contamination is when test answers leak into training data and inflate AI scores. How it happens, how much it distorts results, and how to spot it.

sources.title: Benchmark Contamination | AI360Xpert
sources.snippet: Benchmark contamination occurs when a model's evaluation test set accidentally leaks into its training data. This results in artificially inflated scores because the model is reciting memorized answers rather than demonstrating generalized reasoning.

sources.snippet: Benchmark contamination — Unintended presence of test data or test-adjacent data in a model's training dataset, artificially elevating performance on benchmarks.
